full_judgment:
4. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the decision dated 24.01.2008 passed by the learned Member, Administrative Tribunal No. 3, Dhaka, the respondents preferred Appeal No. 34 of 2008 before the Administrative Appellate Tribunal, Dhaka. The Administrative Appellate Tribunal, upon hearing the parties, by its decision dated 13.01.2009 allowed the appeal on contest setting aside the decision passed by the Administrative Tribunal and dismissed the case on the point of limitation. 

 6. Mr. Syed Mahbubur Rahman, learned Advocate-on-Record, appearing on behalf of the leave petitioner, submits that the Administrative Appellate Tribunal erroneously came to the finding that the case filed by the petitioner before the Administrative Tribunal' was barred by limitation although the petitioner filed the ease within six months as contemplated in the 3rd proviso to section 4 of the Administrative Tribunal Act and as such the impugned decision should be set aside. 

 7. We have considered the submissions of the learned Advocate, perused the impugned decision and the materials on record. It is important to note that the Administrative Tribunal did not frame any issue of whether the case was barred by limitation. 

 8. The Administrative Appellate Tribunal came to the finding that challenging the notification dated 28.02.2003, the petitioner filed the case before the Administrative Tribunal on 29.09.2004, that is, after long six months of statutory period of limitation as laid down in section 4(2) of the Administrative Tribunal Act, 1980. The Administrative Appellate Tribunal found that on 18.01.2004, the petitioner filed an application before the higher authority in the form of an appeal against the notification dated 28.08.2003 and that the petitioner should have filed the case before the Tribunal within eight months from 08.01.2008 and that the case having been filed beyond that period was barred by limitation. 

 15. According to the 2nd proviso, if an appeal or application for review is filed and if the higher administrative authority does not take any decision on such appeal or application for review within two months then such appeal or application for review shall he deemed to have been disallowed after expiry of that period. If the word "disallowed" as mentioned in the 2nd proviso is construed as a decision or order by higher authority as contemplated under the 3rd proviso then there exists a harmonious construction between the 2nd and 3rd provisos and in fact, the legislature intended as such. In that event, the period of computation of limitation of six months as contained in the 3rd proviso be reckoned from the date when an appeal or application for review shall be deemed to have been disallowed as contemplated under the 2nd proviso. The legislature also intended to see that the 2nd and the 3rd provisos are complementary to each other otherwise the 2nd proviso would not have been added before the 3rd proviso by subsequent amendment. Having considered all the 3 provisos, in general, and the provisos 2 and 3, in particular, we find that there is no conflict between the 2nd and the 3rd provisos; rather both the provisos are complementary to each other. 

 21. Therefore, the petitioner should have approached the Administrative Tribunal within 6 (six) months from the date of decision on his Appeal which would be deemed to have been disallowed by the higher administrative authority after two months of its filing as contemplated under the 2nd proviso and the period of limitation of 6 (six) months as mentioned in the 3rd proviso would be reckoned from the expiry of two months as provided under the 2nd proviso. In other words, the petitioner was required to file the appeal within 8 months from the date of filing of the departmental appeal. But the petitioner failed to do so. Consequently, the Administrative Appellate Tribunal rightly came to the finding that the case before the Administrative Tribunal was barred by limitation.
